# 2 Baruch Chapter 31 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Second Fast and Dialogue

---

**31:1** And-I-went-forth from-there and-I-came to-the-people and-I-called-them-together, both-great and-small, and-I-said to-them:

**31:2** Hear O-Israel, and-give-ear O-Jacob — and-be-attentive, all-you-who-sow the-earth:

**31:3** The-sorrow-of-Zion's-mother-[city] and-the-tribulation-of-Jerusalem have-now-come upon-us; behold, both-one-and-the-other-have-been-taken-from-us. But-we-do-not-[need to]-weep over-her adversaries, for-they-are-more-bitter-than-she [is]; and-we-do-not-[need to]-lament over-her enemies, for-they-will-quickly-pass-away.

**31:4** But-do-weep — each-of-you — for-your-own-iniquity; for-on-account-of-that, this-tribulation-has-come upon-you.

**31:5** For-if-you-do-these-things, [namely,] that-you-order your-ways in-righteousness, you-will-depart from-this-age quickly and-not-for-a-long-time.

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Syriac Codex Ambrosianus. Baruch addresses the people after receiving the revelation. The address "Hear O Israel / give ear O Jacob" echoes prophetic invocation forms. The focus shifts from cosmic revelation to pastoral exhortation: weep not for Zion's enemies but for your own sins.*
